lessons.title: Découvrir les sons autour de nous
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify and distinguish between different sounds in their environment using their sense of hearing

opening.activity: Sound mystery walk - students close eyes and listen while teacher makes familiar classroom sounds (pencil sharpener, door closing, water pouring)
materials: various classroom objects that make distinct sounds
opening.visualSupports: ear symbol poster, 'listening detective' badge for each student

main.activity: Sound exploration stations - students rotate through listening activities identifying animal sounds, musical sounds, and nature sounds
materials: audio recordings of different sound categories
main.visualSupports: picture cards matching sounds, sound wave demonstration with ribbon

decisionPoints.question: Are students comfortable closing their eyes to focus on listening?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Extend with blindfolded sound identification games
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use pictures alongside sounds and gradually reduce visual support

decisionPoints.question: Can students identify obvious sounds like dogs barking or cars honking?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Introduce more subtle sounds like leaves rustling or paper tearing
decisionPoints.ifNo: Start with very obvious, contrasting sounds and use visual cues

closing.activity: Sound scavenger hunt - students share one new sound they discovered and demonstrate how to make it safely

troubleshooting.then: Use exaggerated sound contrasts (whisper vs. shout, drum vs. bell) and add visual movement cues

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how we use hearing to stay safe and enjoy music, like hearing car horns or birds singing

lessons.title: Sons forts et sons doux
lessons.oneGoal: Students will compare and contrast loud sounds and soft sounds using descriptive vocabulary

opening.activity: Volume control demonstration - teacher uses voice and simple instruments to show loud and soft, students copy with hand gestures (big gestures for loud, tiny for soft)
materials: simple instruments like shakers or drums
opening.visualSupports: volume meter drawing with big and small sections, hand gesture reference chart

main.activity: Loud and soft exploration with everyday objects - students experiment making loud and soft sounds with paper, blocks, and containers
main.visualSupports: loud/soft comparison chart with pictures, volume gesture reminders

decisionPoints.question: Can students demonstrate volume control with their voices and movements?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Challenge them to create sound stories using different volumes
decisionPoints.ifNo: Practice simple loud/soft copying games with clear visual cues

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand the concept of volume control?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Introduce the idea of appropriate volumes for different situations
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on physical demonstration and imitation without complex explanations

closing.activity: Volume matching game - students listen to sounds and show with body movements whether sounds are loud or soft

troubleshooting.then: Use visual volume meter and practice with fun activities like 'mouse voice' and 'giant voice'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning to adjust our voices for different situations, like whispering in libraries or calling friends outside

lessons.title: Sons aigus et sons graves
lessons.oneGoal: Students will distinguish between high-pitched and low-pitched sounds through listening activities

opening.activity: Voice pitch exploration - students practice making mouse squeaks (high) and bear growls (low) while using hand gestures (high hands for high sounds, low hands for low sounds)
opening.visualSupports: high/low animal poster, pitch hand signals chart

main.activity: Pitch discovery with xylophone and bottles - students explore how different sized objects make different pitch sounds
materials: glass bottles with different amounts of water
main.visualSupports: high/low pitch chart with visual height differences, musical note representations

decisionPoints.question: Can students distinguish between obvious high and low pitches?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Introduce middle pitches and create simple three-note patterns
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use very contrasting examples like whistle vs. drum and add visual height cues

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for hands-on exploration with instruments?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let them experiment freely with creating high and low sounds
decisionPoints.ifNo: Demonstrate first and have students identify pitch before hands-on time

closing.activity: High-low sound sorting - students categorize picture cards of things that make high sounds vs. low sounds

troubleshooting.then: Use extreme examples (baby cry vs. motorcycle) and combine with visual height demonstrations

lessons.realWorldConnection: Recognizing different voices (mom's low voice, baby's high voice) and animal sounds (bird tweets, cow moos)

lessons.title: D'où viennent les sons?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify that sounds come from vibrating objects and sources around them

opening.activity: Mystery sound investigation - students guess what's making sounds behind a screen, then reveal sources to make connection between objects and sounds
opening.visualSupports: sound source matching cards, detective badge for each student

main.activity: Vibration discovery with rubber bands, tuning forks, and drums - students observe and feel vibrations while sounds are produced
materials: rice or small beads to show vibration
main.visualSupports: vibration demonstration setup, before/during/after pictures of vibrating objects

decisionPoints.question: Can students see visible vibrations in drums with rice or rubber bands stretching?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Introduce the connection between vibration speed and pitch
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use more obvious examples like large drums with beads jumping

decisionPoints.question: Are students interested in exploring how vibrations create sound?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let them experiment with different objects to find vibrations
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on dramatic demonstrations and let them feel vibrations in their own throat

closing.activity: Vibration hunt - students find three objects in the classroom that vibrate when they make sounds

troubleshooting.then: Have them feel their throat while humming and use very visual examples like drums with rice

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that speakers vibrate to make music and our throat vibrates when we talk

lessons.title: Sentir les vibrations
lessons.oneGoal: Students will safely feel vibrations while sounds are being produced using hands-on exploration

opening.activity: Vibration body exploration - students feel vibrations in their chest when humming, throat when talking, and head when singing
materials: mirrors for students to see mouth movements
opening.visualSupports: body vibration diagram showing throat, chest, and head

main.activity: Safe vibration exploration stations - students feel vibrations through desks when tapping, rulers when plucking, and balloon surfaces when playing music nearby
main.visualSupports: safety reminder chart for touching, vibration exploration recording sheet

decisionPoints.question: Are students comfortable and safe feeling vibrations with their hands?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Introduce more subtle vibrations like feeling music through tables
decisionPoints.ifNo: Start with obvious vibrations they can see and gradually add touching

decisionPoints.question: Can students connect feeling vibrations with hearing sounds?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Challenge them to predict whether objects will vibrate before testing
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simultaneous feeling and hearing with clear examples

closing.activity: Vibration sharing circle - students demonstrate their favorite vibration discovery and explain what they felt

troubleshooting.then: Use stronger vibrations like large drums or have them hold balloons near speakers

lessons.realWorldConnection: Feeling the vibrations in a guitar or piano when someone plays, or feeling our chest when we sing loudly

lessons.title: Fabriquer un téléphone à ficelle
lessons.oneGoal: Students will construct and test a simple string telephone to explore how sound travels

opening.activity: Communication challenge - students try to communicate across the room using whispers, then discover they need a better way
opening.visualSupports: communication problem poster, telephone invention story pictures

main.activity: String telephone construction and testing - students work in pairs to build telephones with cups and string, then test communication
main.visualSupports: step-by-step construction visual guide, troubleshooting tips poster

decisionPoints.question: Can students successfully construct their telephones with minimal help?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let them experiment with different string lengths and cup sizes
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide pre-punched cups and cut strings, focus on testing and using

decisionPoints.question: Do the string telephones work for clear communication?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Challenge students to send secret messages and test maximum distance
decisionPoints.ifNo: Troubleshoot together: check string tension, cup contact, and speaking technique

closing.activity: Telephone testing celebration - pairs demonstrate their telephones and share the coolest message they sent

troubleshooting.then: Check that string is tight, cups aren't touching anything, and students speak directly into cup

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how phones and communication devices help us talk to people far away

lessons.title: Explorer les tambours
lessons.oneGoal: Students will investigate how different sizes and materials affect drum sounds through experimentation

opening.activity: Drum circle rhythm - students use body percussion (clapping, patting) to create rhythms together before exploring drum instruments
opening.visualSupports: rhythm pattern posters, drum circle formation diagram

main.activity: Drum making and testing station - students create drums using containers of different sizes and various covering materials, then compare sounds
main.visualSupports: drum construction steps poster, size and sound comparison chart

decisionPoints.question: Can students hear clear differences between drums of different sizes?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Introduce rhythm creation and pattern making with their drums
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use very different sized containers and help them focus on one sound at a time

decisionPoints.question: Are students successful at constructing their own drums?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let them experiment with different covering materials and decorating
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide pre-made drums and focus on sound exploration and rhythm

closing.activity: Drum concert - students use their handmade drums to create a simple group rhythm performance

troubleshooting.then: Use very contrasting drum sizes and have them feel vibrations as well as listen

lessons.realWorldConnection: Connecting to music and rhythm in different cultures, like drums in celebrations and parades

lessons.title: Construire un kazoo
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create a kazoo instrument and explore how their voice creates vibrations and sound

opening.activity: Voice exploration - students experiment with different voice sounds (humming, buzzing, singing) while feeling throat vibrations
opening.visualSupports: voice production diagram, different voice sounds example chart

main.activity: Kazoo construction and voice modification exploration - students build kazoos from toilet paper tubes and wax paper, then explore how it changes their voice
main.visualSupports: kazoo construction step-by-step guide, voice modification explanation pictures

decisionPoints.question: Can students successfully make sounds through their completed kazoos?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage them to try different songs and voice pitches with the kazoo
decisionPoints.ifNo: Check wax paper tension and demonstrate proper humming technique

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand how their voice vibrations create the kazoo sound?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Have them experiment with different vocal techniques and observe changes
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on feeling throat vibrations while using kazoo and making direct connections

closing.activity: Kazoo orchestra - students use their kazoos to hum a simple familiar song together

troubleshooting.then: Ensure wax paper is secure but not too tight, and demonstrate proper humming not blowing

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how musical instruments help us make music and express ourselves creatively

lessons.title: Bouteilles musicales
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create musical bottles with different water levels to produce different pitches

opening.activity: Water level prediction - students predict what will happen to sound when water levels change in bottles
materials: clear bottles with different amounts of water
opening.visualSupports: water level and pitch prediction chart, before/after comparison setup

main.activity: Musical bottle construction and pitch exploration - students create sets of bottles with different water levels and explore pitch changes
main.visualSupports: step-by-step bottle filling guide, pitch progression visual chart

decisionPoints.question: Can students hear clear pitch differences between bottles with different water levels?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Challenge them to create simple melodies or arrange bottles from low to high pitch
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use more dramatic water level differences and help them focus on one bottle at a time

decisionPoints.question: Are students successful with water filling and measurement?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let them experiment with precise measurements and create specific pitches
decisionPoints.ifNo: Pre-fill bottles to different levels and focus on sound exploration

closing.activity: Bottle band performance - small groups use their bottle sets to play simple tunes or create musical conversations

troubleshooting.then: Use very different water levels, tap gently, and have students hum along to feel the pitch

lessons.realWorldConnection: Connecting to how different sized instruments make different sounds, like piccolo vs. tuba

lessons.title: Maracas et shakers
lessons.oneGoal: Students will construct shaker instruments using various materials to explore how contents affect sound quality

opening.activity: Shaker sound mystery - students listen to different pre-made shakers and guess what might be inside each one
opening.visualSupports: shaker contents guessing chart, different materials picture cards

main.activity: Maracas construction with material experimentation - students create shakers using various filling materials and compare sound qualities
main.visualSupports: shaker construction steps, material and sound quality comparison chart

decisionPoints.question: Can students identify how different materials create different shaker sounds?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let them experiment with mixing materials or varying amounts
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on very different materials (rice vs. pebbles) and clear sound demonstrations

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for independent construction and decoration?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage creative decoration and personalization of their shakers
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide assembly assistance and focus on sound exploration activities

closing.activity: Shaker rhythm celebration - students create group rhythms using their different-sounding shakers

troubleshooting.then: Use very contrasting materials and have students shake one at a time to focus listening

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding rhythm instruments in music and how different materials make different sounds in daily life

lessons.title: Guitare en boîte
lessons.oneGoal: Students will build a simple box guitar with rubber bands to explore string vibrations and pitch

opening.activity: String vibration demonstration - students pluck individual rubber bands of different sizes to hear and see vibration differences
opening.visualSupports: string vibration slow-motion demonstration, pitch and tension connection chart

main.activity: Box guitar construction and string exploration - students create guitars using boxes and rubber bands, then explore how tension affects pitch
main.visualSupports: guitar construction step-by-step guide, string tension and pitch relationship diagram

decisionPoints.question: Can students successfully stretch rubber bands and create different pitches?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Teach them simple fingering techniques to create different notes
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on strumming all strings together and feeling vibrations

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand how tightness affects the pitch of their guitar strings?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let them experiment with tuning their guitars and creating melodies
decisionPoints.ifNo: Demonstrate with one string at a time, showing loose vs. tight comparisons

closing.activity: Guitar showcase - students take turns playing their box guitars and sharing their favorite sound discovery

troubleshooting.then: Ensure rubber bands are properly secured and demonstrate gentle plucking technique

lessons.realWorldConnection: Connecting to real guitars, violins, and other string instruments in music and how they work

lessons.title: Flûte de Pan avec pailles
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create a panpipe instrument using straws to demonstrate how length affects pitch

opening.activity: Straw length investigation - students blow across straws of different lengths to discover pitch changes before construction
opening.visualSupports: length and pitch relationship demonstration, wind instrument pictures

main.activity: Pan flute construction and melody creation - students create panpipes by arranging straws of different lengths and explore making melodies
main.visualSupports: pan flute construction guide, length arrangement patterns, simple melody visual guides

decisionPoints.question: Can students create clear pitch differences with their straw lengths?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Teach them to play simple tunes and create musical conversations
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on making sounds and use pre-cut straws with very obvious length differences

decisionPoints.question: Are students able to successfully blow across straws to create sounds?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage experimentation with breath control and different playing techniques
decisionPoints.ifNo: Demonstrate proper blowing technique and provide individual support

closing.activity: Pan flute orchestra - students combine their instruments to create group musical experiences

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: creating sounds with the pan flute
troubleshooting.then: Check straw positioning and demonstrate gentle side-blowing technique, not direct blowing

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how flutes, recorders, and organ pipes work by changing air column length

lessons.title: Orchestre de la classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students will combine all their handmade instruments to create a class orchestra and perform together

opening.activity: Instrument review parade - students walk around with their favorite handmade instrument, demonstrating its sound and sharing how it works
opening.visualSupports: instrument family classification chart, orchestra setup diagram

main.activity: Orchestra formation and collaborative music making - students organize into instrument sections and practice playing together
main.visualSupports: orchestra seating chart, simple rhythm and melody notation, conductor signal guide

decisionPoints.question: Can students coordinate their instruments to play together as a group?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Introduce simple conducting signals and try performing different musical styles
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on taking turns by instrument groups and keeping steady rhythms together

decisionPoints.question: Are students engaged and excited about their orchestra experience?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let them compose their own group songs and take turns conducting
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on fun, familiar songs and ensure every student feels successful with their contribution

closing.activity: Orchestra reflection circle - students share their favorite moment from playing in the orchestra and what they learned about teamwork in music

troubleshooting.then: Use clear visual cues for start/stop and practice with one instrument section at a time

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how orchestras and bands work together to create beautiful music performances

lessons.title: Concert de démonstration
lessons.oneGoal: Students will demonstrate their understanding of sound and vibration by performing and explaining their instruments

opening.activity: Concert preparation - students practice their performance pieces and prepare simple explanations of how their instruments work
opening.visualSupports: concert program with student names and instruments, science explanation prompt cards

main.activity: Student concert performance with scientific explanations - students perform with their instruments and explain the science behind how they create sound
main.visualSupports: performance order chart, scientific vocabulary reminder posters, applause and encouragement signs

decisionPoints.question: Are students confident and ready to perform for an audience?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Invite other classes or family members to attend the concert
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep the audience small and supportive, focus on celebrating effort rather than performance

decisionPoints.question: Can students explain the science concepts behind their instruments?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage detailed explanations about vibration, pitch, and volume
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use simple prompts like 'This makes sound when...' and support with gestures

closing.activity: Concert celebration and reflection - students receive certificates and share what they're most proud of learning about sound and music

troubleshooting.then: Pair nervous students with confident partners and use visual cues to support explanations

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that musicians share their music with others and can explain how their instruments work

lessons.title: Sons dans la nature
lessons.oneGoal: Students will apply their sound knowledge to identify and classify natural sounds during outdoor exploration

opening.activity: Nature sound preparation - students listen to recordings of natural sounds and predict what they might hear during outdoor exploration
opening.visualSupports: nature sound identification cards, outdoor safety reminder chart

main.activity: Outdoor sound expedition - students explore school grounds or nearby natural area to identify, record, and classify natural sounds
main.visualSupports: sound classification categories (animal, weather, plant, water), observation recording templates

decisionPoints.question: Can students identify and classify different categories of natural sounds?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Challenge them to find the sources of mysterious sounds and investigate how natural sounds are made
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on obvious sounds like birds chirping and wind in trees, using clear categories

decisionPoints.question: Are students engaged and focused during the outdoor exploration?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Extend the exploration time and let them discover unexpected sound sources
decisionPoints.ifNo: Structure with specific sound-finding missions and shorter exploration periods

closing.activity: Nature sound sharing - students report their discoveries and create a class list of all the natural sounds they identified

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: focusing on listening during outdoor exploration
troubleshooting.then: Use quiet listening challenges and have students close eyes periodically to focus on hearing

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how animals, wind, and water create sounds in nature and how we can enjoy natural music

lessons.title: Échos et réflexion du son
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore how sounds bounce back to create echoes in different environments

opening.activity: Echo demonstration - students experience echoes in different school locations like hallways, gymnasiums, or outdoor areas with buildings
opening.visualSupports: echo demonstration pictures, sound wave bouncing diagram

main.activity: Echo investigation in various school environments - students test making sounds in different locations and observe echo effects
main.visualSupports: echo timing chart, sound reflection explanation pictures

decisionPoints.question: Can students clearly hear and identify echoes in different environments?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Investigate how distance and surface materials affect echo quality
decisionPoints.ifNo: Start with very obvious echo locations and use sharp, clear sounds like hand claps

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand that echoes are sounds bouncing back?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore how animals like bats use echoes for navigation
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use physical demonstrations with bouncing balls to show sound bouncing concept

closing.activity: Echo experiment reporting - students share their discoveries about where echoes work best and why

troubleshooting.then: Use very obvious echo locations and have students count time between original sound and echo

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding echoes in tunnels, mountains, and large buildings, and how some animals use echoes to navigate

lessons.title: Musique du monde
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore instruments and musical sounds from different cultures around the world

opening.activity: World music listening tour - students listen to musical examples from different cultures and identify familiar and unfamiliar instruments
opening.visualSupports: world map with musical traditions, instrument pictures from different cultures

main.activity: Cultural instrument exploration and creation - students explore examples of instruments from various cultures and create their own versions
main.visualSupports: cultural instrument classification chart, respectful cultural learning guidelines

decisionPoints.question: Are students respectful and curious about different cultural musical traditions?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore how different cultures use music for celebrations and storytelling
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on the beauty and creativity of different musical sounds rather than cultural differences

decisionPoints.question: Can students identify similarities and differences between cultural instruments and their own creations?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Discuss how all cultures create music and express themselves through sound
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on enjoying the different sounds and connecting to their own musical experiences

closing.activity: World music appreciation circle - students share what they found most interesting about music from different cultures

troubleshooting.then: Focus on the joy of different musical sounds and connect to students' own family musical traditions

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that people around the world create music with different instruments and traditions

lessons.title: Inventions sonores créatives
lessons.oneGoal: Students will design and create their own original sound-making device using recycled materials

opening.activity: Inventor inspiration - students brainstorm what kind of new sound they want to create and look at recycled materials for possibilities
opening.visualSupports: invention process poster, famous inventor examples, creative thinking prompts

main.activity: Original instrument invention and testing - students design, build, and test their own unique sound-making inventions
materials: variety of recycled containers, materials, and tools
construction supplies like tape and glue
main.visualSupports: invention planning template, troubleshooting guide for inventors

decisionPoints.question: Are students successfully creating original sounds with their inventions?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage them to refine their designs and explore multiple sound possibilities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide more structured guidance and suggest specific material combinations

decisionPoints.question: Do students show creative thinking and problem-solving in their inventions?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Challenge them to solve specific sound problems or create instruments for specific purposes
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide more examples and support collaborative invention process

closing.activity: Inventor showcase - students present their sound inventions and explain their design thinking

troubleshooting.then: Pair students for collaborative inventing and provide step-by-step construction support

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that inventors and musicians create new instruments and that we can be creative problem solvers

lessons.title: Enregistrer nos créations
lessons.oneGoal: Students will record their musical creations and listen back to evaluate their sound productions

opening.activity: Recording studio setup - students learn how recording technology works and practice using simple recording devices
opening.visualSupports: recording studio pictures, recording process step-by-step guide

main.activity: Musical creation recording and playback analysis - students record performances with their instruments and analyze their recordings
main.visualSupports: recording quality checklist, listening and evaluation guides

decisionPoints.question: Are students successfully operating recording technology independently?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let them experiment with different recording techniques and multiple takes
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide partner support and focus on simple recording and playback experiences

decisionPoints.question: Can students thoughtfully evaluate and improve their recorded performances?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage them to make multiple recordings and choose their best versions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on enjoying listening to themselves and identifying what they like about their music

closing.activity: Recording listening party - students share their favorite recorded creations with the class

troubleshooting.then: Simplify the technology or have students work in pairs with peer support

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how musicians record music and how we can use technology to save and share our creative work

lessons.oneGoal: Students will organize and participate in a celebration showcasing all their sound and music learning

opening.activity: Festival preparation - students help set up different stations showcasing their learning and prepare to be teachers for visitors
opening.visualSupports: festival map and station guide, student teacher preparation cards

main.activity: Sound and vibration festival with community celebration - students lead interactive stations teaching visitors about sound science and demonstrating their instruments
main.visualSupports: festival program, station instruction cards, learning celebration banners

decisionPoints.question: Are students confident in teaching others about their sound learning?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Let them lead interactive demonstrations and answer visitor questions independently
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide supportive adult partners and focus on demonstrating rather than explaining

decisionPoints.question: Is the festival creating a joyful celebration of learning for everyone?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage student leadership in organizing activities and welcoming visitors
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on structured, successful activities that highlight student accomplishments

closing.activity: Festival reflection and celebration - students share their proudest learning moments and celebrate their growth as sound scientists

troubleshooting.then: Provide simple scripts or partner students with confident peers for support

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that communities celebrate music and learning together, and that we can share our knowledge with others

familyConnections.unitLetter:
Chers parents et familles,

Nous sommes ravis de commencer notre nouvelle unité: ""

Cette unité permettra à votre enfant de:
• Explorer des concepts importants en sciences
• Développer du vocabulaire en français
• Pratiquer de nouvelles compétences
• Faire des connexions avec la vie quotidienne

Quelques thèmes que nous explorerons:
Découvrir les sons autour de nous, Sons forts et sons doux, Sons aigus et sons graves, D'où viennent les sons?, Sentir les vibrations

Comment vous pouvez aider à la maison:
• Demandez à votre enfant de partager ce qu'il/elle a appris
• Pratiquez le nouveau vocabulaire ensemble (voir la liste ci-jointe)
• Essayez les activités suggérées quand vous avez du temps
• Célébrez les efforts et les progrès, pas seulement les résultats

Encouragez les questions 'pourquoi' et explorez ensemble les réponses.

N'hésitez pas à me contacter si vous avez des questions ou si vous souhaitez partager des ressources culturelles liées à cette unité.

La curiosité scientifique commence à la maison!

Cordialement,
[Nom de l'enseignant(e)]
